_doc: THE RELEASE FAMILIES (AGENTS.md part 4, 'A release rebuilds and re-records only the families that changed', Andrew 2026-11-28).
Every binding a release ships (bindings/development_groups.json, bindings/merged_groups.json members, the release rows of
tools/release_reuse.py) and every verify lane (tools/identity_columns.py lanes --scope all) belongs to exactly one family.
tools/release_families.py reads this file; `python3 tools/release_families.py check` refuses a binding or a lane with no family.
A family is REUSED whole (the previous release's bytes and its recorded columns) only when every binding identity in it is
unchanged (tools/release_reuse.py identity) AND no merged file it shares with a BUILD family is rebuilt; otherwise it BUILDS
whole and its lanes record on every device. `shared` is the core every family loads: when it builds, every lane records.
A host binding sits with its device twin (`_mojolearn_x` and `_mojolearn_x_host`); the `_m1` Metal 1 builds take their
binding's family. The binding families follow the host owners of the 2026-11-07 split (docs/build/HOT_GROUPS.md section 6).
LANES. `lanes` maps a lane to its family explicitly; `lane_rules` are fnmatch patterns tried in order for a lane `lanes` does not
name. The lanes are WRITTEN BY CODE, never by reading names: `python3 tools/release_families.py derive --write` assigns each lane
the one non-shared family of the bindings it loads (tools/lane_select.py lane_sources: the bindings and declared host routes of
the lane), and `shared` when it loads none or bindings of several families. Until that has run, the one rule `*` -> shared
holds: every lane records whenever any family records (the safe superset; no family keeps a column). `check --lanes` refuses
an explicit lane whose loaded bindings leave its family and shared.
MERGED FILES (2026-11-28, lane family-groups-1). No merged file of bindings/merged_groups.json holds bindings of two families,
on any directory set or macOS <stem>_m1 file; `check` refuses one that does. A family's build then rebuilds only its own files.
`_mojolearn_tokenizer_host` is `shared`, not tokenizer: it is the host owner every runtime owner binding is connected into
(python/mojolearn/host_surface.py HOST_IMPORT_ALIASES) and it registers the attribute, parameter, constructor, array, optimizer
and embedding-layer entries every family's estimators call, so every lane loads it. `_mojolearn_runtime_family_host` (kernel)
also carries the clustering and density doors and `_mojolearn_runtime_trees_host` (trees) the density, neighbor-predict and
archive doors: a lane that loads one of them with another family's binding is a `shared` lane (derive), which is safe.
PYTHON GLUE. `python.rules` are fnmatch patterns over the tracked files under `python.root`, tried in order; the first match gives
the file's family, and `-` means the file is not product glue. A family whose Python files changed since the previous release
RECORDS its lanes although its binaries are reused; a changed `shared` file records every lane. `check` refuses a file no rule
matches, a family file that another family's or a shared file imports, and a family file that names another family's binding.
`-` is the verification tooling and what is not code: tests/, verify_reference/, reference_cards/, the `_verify*` and
`_verification_*` modules, the command line (`__main__.py`, `_identity.py`, `_check_both.py`, `_conformance.py`), the verifier's
device inventory and fixtures (`_gpu_witness.py`, `_causal_lm_fixtures.py`, `_tokenizer_synthetic.py`), the Markdown and notice
files, and `_version.py` (the version string alone, which changes every release). Everything else is glue. A file is given a
family only when every public name in it loads a binding of that family and nothing outside the family imports it; the glue is
cross-linked today (`_classical_host.py`, `_parallel_neural.py`, the `_expansion_*` modules import across families), so most of
it is `shared`.
